items.item: NOT TESTED — Could not be verified.
NOT APPLICABLE — Not relevant to the current project phase.
Game starts correctly from a new installation.
All game data has valid identifiers.
Approved reference exists in the project.
All current saltwater fish artwork follows the reference.
VIP preview artwork is visually consistent.
Sprites are not blurry at gameplay scale.
Colors are vivid but appropriate to species.
No generic placeholder shapes are presented as finished artwork.
Every species has a unique internal ID.
Every species has an appropriate common name.
Scientific names are recorded where applicable.
Designer morphs are distinguished from biological species.
Every implemented species has a working sprite.
Every implemented species can be displayed correctly.
Planned species are not marked implemented.
Juveniles are visually distinct from adults.
Baby fish are not merely shrunken adult sprites.
Designer morph artwork changes at biologically appropriate stages.
Unnecessary duplicated sprite assets are avoided.
Dead artwork remains recognizable as the correct species.
Sprite asset paths remain valid after saving/loading.
Eyes remain attached to the head.
Eyes are visible in the appropriate side profile.
Eyes remain correctly positioned when facing left.
Eyes remain correctly positioned when facing right.
Eye layers render in the correct order.
Eye pixels are not accidentally cropped.
Eye correctness has been reviewed across all implemented fish.
Fish face left when swimming left.
Fish face right when swimming right.
Fish do not continuously flicker between directions.
Fish do not pass through solid rocks.
Sprite flipping does not mirror UI text.
Animation does not detach body parts.
Fish movement remains smooth at different frame rates.
Designer varieties reference their correct biological species.
Varieties are not misrepresented as separate species.
Pattern artwork matches its intended variety.
Eye and swimming rules are satisfied.
Species and variety counts are accurate.
No new freshwater fish were added unintentionally.
No freshwater bottom feeders were added.
No freshwater breeding systems were expanded.
Existing freshwater species data was preserved.
Shared UI changes do not damage freshwater systems.
Saltwater and freshwater catalogs remain separated.
Freshwater store navigation does not authorize freshwater content development.
Exposed skeleton for applicable stony corals.
Coral animations are subtle and natural.
Coral sprites do not look like generic shapes.
All coral art matches the approved reference.
Placement requires a valid surface or mounting structure.
Glass-mounted racks or other valid supports work.
Coral placement inside solid rock is rejected.
Coral placement outside the aquarium is rejected.
Moving a rock moves attached corals correctly.
Removing a rock cannot leave floating corals.
Changing sand depth revalidates relevant coral placement.
Each category has recognizable visual differences.
Coral attachments to rocks remain valid.
Dry and live rock states are distinguished where supported.
Rock artwork matches the approved visual style.
Sand can be added to empty tanks.
Required mass scales with aquarium floor area.
Sand depth changes the tank's visual profile.
Sand reduces effective water volume appropriately.
Substrate depth affects appropriate habitat checks.
No arbitrary bonuses are assigned solely from geographical sand names.
Sand develops biological maturation over time.
Cyanobacterial growth is distinguished from true algae.
Growth responds to grazing organisms where implemented.
Algae does not appear solely because a fixed timer elapsed.
Substrate remains visually clean under suitable conditions.
Deep sand disturbance risks are condition-dependent.
Rock placement is supported during appropriate setup stages.
Readiness is based on actual conditions.
Fish cannot be introduced when critical conditions are unsafe.
Setup guidance explains the next action.
Tank readiness uses actual water values.
Buoyancy and current affect corpse movement.
Dead fish cannot reproduce or be sold as living fish.
Death from severe predation or aggression.
Predation does not behave randomly without triggers.
Aquarium remains visible behind dark overlay.
Background clicks do not affect the tank.
X button is in the top-right corner.
Closing does not reload the game.
Opening repeatedly does not duplicate windows.
Switching main tabs preserves selected aquarium.
Purchasing does not automatically switch tanks.
Player may choose another eligible destination.
An unsafe aquarium cannot receive livestock through a purchase bypass.
Equipment goes to the correct destination or inventory.
Rock goes to correct destination or inventory.
Sand goes to correct destination or inventory.
Coral placement still requires suitable surface.
Destination-related state persists correctly after saving.
Freshwater animals cannot accidentally enter a marine tank.
Saltwater animals cannot accidentally enter a freshwater tank.
Living livestock is not stored indefinitely in invalid inventory.
Empty categories have honest empty states.
No freshwater content was added during the current phase.
Previously acquired event items remain owned.
Aquarium is the main visual centerpiece.
UI remains usable at smaller desktop resolutions.
Long absence does not cause unintended save corruption.
Chemistry calculations are not performed unnecessarily every frame.
Sprite atlases or equivalent batching are used appropriately.
Static scenery is cached where useful.
Offscreen aquariums are not fully rendered unnecessarily.
Fish remain visually clear under lower graphics settings.
Long-running simulation does not cause progressive slowdown.
Frame rate is measured rather than assumed.
Every added species has unique metadata.
Every added species follows art-stage requirements.
Every added fish follows eye/direction rules.
Every added coral follows placement restrictions.
Every added species has appropriate care difficulty.
No freshwater livestock expansion occurs without authorization.
Special approved expansions, such as the clownfish collection, are clearly identified as exceptions.
Uses one primary section per major mechanic.
Records the latest approved art reference.
Includes the store destination aquarium rule.
